symbols.name: \eta_\infty

symbols.name: J
symbols.def: Terminally measurable label selecting the attained fixed attractor.

symbols.name: \mathcal J

symbols.name: \Gamma_P

symbols.name: \Omega_J

symbols.name: V_\infty
symbols.def: Terminal estimator covariance \(V_\infty=H^{-1}\Omega_\infty H^{-\top}\).

symbols.name: Z_1

symbols.name: s_\eta

symbols.name: p_-

symbols.name: p_j

symbols.name: \mathcal H_T

symbols.name: \omega_{c,T}
symbols.def: Deterministic horizon-specific lower bound for the early-measurable directional information scale.

symbols.name: \mathcal E_T

symbols.name: \widehat V_T

symbols.name: \Lambda_T

symbols.name: \mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)
symbols.def: Early-stabilized projected adaptive IPW-Z law class at horizon \(T\) for the prespecified nonzero contrast \(c\).

symbols.name: J_T
symbols.def: For \(k_T\ge1\), the fixed-tie-broken nearest-attractor label to \(k_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{k_T}\eta_{t-1}\); set to \(1\) when \(k_T=0\).

assumptions.condition: The vectors \(W_1,\ldots,W_T\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P\).
Conditional on \(X_t\) and \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\), the action \(A_t\) is drawn from the logged distribution \(\pi_t(\cdot\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\) independently of \((Y_t(a))_{a\in\mathcal A}\).
For every \(a\in\mathcal A\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(\eta\in\mathsf H\), the policy satisfies \(\Pi(a\mid x,\eta)\ge\varepsilon\).
The common envelope satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A,\theta\in\Theta}\|g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\|_2\le B\) almost surely.
constants: \(B<\infty\), fixed across every horizon and member law

assumptions.condition: The map \(\theta\mapsto g(a,x,y;\theta)\) is continuously differentiable on a common open neighborhood of \(\operatorname{conv}(\Theta)\), with \(\|\partial_\theta g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_1\) there, and is twice continuously differentiable on the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), with \(\|\partial_\theta^2 g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_2\) throughout that ball.
constants: \(D_1,D_2<\infty\) and \(\rho>0\), fixed across every horizon and member law
\(\kappa(u)>0\) for every \(u>0\), fixed across every horizon and member law

standard.name: Uniform separation of a Z-functional root

constants: \(s_\Theta>0\), fixed across every horizon and member law
\(h_->0\), fixed across every horizon and member law

assumptions.condition: The common policy modulus satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A,x\in\mathcal X}|\Pi(a\mid x,\eta)-\Pi(a\mid x,\eta')|\le L_\Pi\|\eta-\eta'\|_2\) for all \(\eta,\eta'\in\mathsf H\).
constants: \(L_\Pi<\infty\), fixed across every horizon and member law

assumptions.condition: There exists a \(\sigma(\bigcup_{t\ge1}\mathcal F_t)\)-measurable \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\)-valued random variable \(J\) such that \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J\) almost surely.

novel.justification: This atomic condition selects one of finitely many fixed terminal states without imposing pointwise convergence of the policy state.
This single Cesaro relation is the only path-approximation restriction and supplies a falsifiable common triangular-array modulus without imposing pointwise state convergence.

assumptions.condition: The common deterministic error envelope satisfies \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\to0\).

novel.justification: The common envelope is a proposal-specific class-level restriction. Over \(\mathfrak Q_T\), it has only a numerical approximation and root-localization role for the IPW--Z estimator; over \(\mathfrak P_T\), it additionally combines the Cesaro policy-state approximation error and attraction-failure probability. Mourrat supplies only the martingale central-limit ingredient used after the applicable envelope is imposed.

assumptions.condition: The terminal covariance satisfies \(\Omega_\infty\succeq\omega_-I_d\) almost surely.
constants: \(\omega_->0\), fixed across every horizon and member law

novel.justification: A common almost-sure lower eigenvalue bound for the terminal random covariance is the proposal-specific uniform variance-growth primitive. The matching upper bound is derived from policy-wide overlap and the bounded score, not assumed.

This proposal-specific condition requires relative suffix predictable-QV approximation to an information scale fixed by the early filtration; the explicit obstruction shows that lower growth without this measurability boundary is insufficient.

definitions.name: finite-tail-attractor adaptive-experiment class
definitions.construction: For fixed \(m\), \(\bar\eta_1,\ldots,\bar\eta_m\), \(s_\eta\), \(p_-\), \(\varepsilon,B,D_1,D_2,h_-,L_\Pi,\omega_-,\kappa,s_\Theta,\rho\), and common sequences \((r_T,\delta_T)_{T\ge1}\), define \(\mathfrak P_T\) to be the set of laws \(P\) that, at horizon \(T\), satisfy every condition in \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}full\text{-}data},\ldots,\mathrm{ass:basin\text{-}nondegeneracy}\) with these common objects, envelopes, and moduli. The fixed states obey \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}attractor\text{-}separation}\), the terminal label and selected state obey \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}tail\text{-}selection}\), every label obeys \(\mathrm{ass:basin\text{-}mass\text{-}floor}\), and the path approximation is supplied solely by \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}attraction\text{-}modulus}\). Thus \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J\), every one of the \(m\) separated basins has mass at least \(p_-\), and the policy path is approximated by its selected attractor only through the uniform Cesaro inequality. Pointwise convergence of \(\eta_t\) is not imposed.

definitions.name: adaptive IPW-Z estimator
definitions.construction: First choose a measurable preliminary estimator \(\widetilde\theta_T\in\Theta\) satisfying \(\|G_T(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2\le\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)\|_2+T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T)\), using a fixed measurable tie-breaking rule. Define the compact correspondence \(\mathcal Z_T=\{\theta\in\Theta:G_T(\theta)=0,\ \|\theta-\widetilde\theta_T\|_2\le\rho/2\}\) and \(E_T=\{\mathcal Z_T\ne\varnothing\}\). Continuity of \(G_T\) on compact \(\Theta\) makes \(\mathcal Z_T\) compact, and its standard joint measurability permits a fixed measurable lexicographic compact-set selector. On \(E_T\), let \(\widehat\theta_T\) be that selected member of \(\mathcal Z_T\); on \(E_T^c\), set \(\widehat\theta_T=\widetilde\theta_T\).

definitions.name: bounded two-state separation witness
definitions.construction: For every \(T\ge2\), let \(P^{\dagger}\) be the law with \(K=3\), \(d=2\), \(\Theta=[-1,1]^2\), \(\theta^*=0\), a singleton \(\mathcal X\), and constant \(X_t\). Independently across \(t\) and between arms, let \(Y_t(1)\) be equiprobable on \(\{-\sqrt{2/5},\sqrt{2/5}\}\), let \(Y_t(2)\) be equiprobable on \(\{-\sqrt{1/2},\sqrt{1/2}\}\), and set \(Y_t(3)=0\). Set \(g(1,x,y;\theta)=(y-\theta_1,0)^\top\), \(g(2,x,y;\theta)=(0,y-\theta_2)^\top\), and \(g(3,x,y;\theta)=0\). Take \(m=2\), \(q=1\), \(\mathsf H=[0,1]\), \(\bar\eta_1=0\), \(\bar\eta_2=1\), and linearly interpolate the context-free policy between \(\Pi(\cdot\mid x,0)=(2/5,1/4,7/20)\) and \(\Pi(\cdot\mid x,1)=(2/5,1/6,13/30)\). Start at \(\eta_0=1/2\), set \(J=1\) if and only if \(A_1=1\), set \(J=2\) otherwise, define \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J=J-1\), and put \(\eta_t=\eta_\infty\) for every \(t\ge1\).

definitions.name: terminal-representative covariance
definitions.construction:
For \(\eta\in\mathsf H\), define
\[
 \Gamma_P(\eta)=E_P\!\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \frac{g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta^*)g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta^*)^\top}
 {\Pi(a\mid X_t,\eta)}\right].
\]
For every \(j\in\mathcal J=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), set
\[
 p_j=P(J=j),\qquad
 \Omega_j=\Gamma_P(\bar\eta_j),\qquad
 V_j=H^{-1}\Omega_jH^{-\top}.
\]
Define
\[
 \Omega_J=\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbf1\{J=j\}\Omega_j,\qquad
 V_J=\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbf1\{J=j\}V_j,
\]
and set
\[
 \Omega_\infty=\Gamma_P(\eta_\infty),\qquad
 V_\infty=H^{-1}\Omega_\infty H^{-\top}.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}tail\text{-}selection}\), substitution of \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J\) gives \(\Omega_\infty=\Omega_J\) and \(V_\infty=V_J\) almost surely.

definitions.name: contrast-specific early-scale event-truncated realized-QV sandwich
definitions.construction:
Set
\[
 \widehat\Omega_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\widehat\xi_t\widehat\xi_t^\top,
 \qquad
 \mathcal H_T=\{\sigma_{\min}(\widehat H_T)\ge h_-/2\}.
\]
Define the total nonnegative scalar
\[
 \widehat q_T(c)=
 \begin{cases}
 c^\top\widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top}c,
   &\text{on }\mathcal H_T,\\
 0,&\text{on }\mathcal H_T^c,
 \end{cases}
\]
where the inverse is evaluated only on \(\mathcal H_T\), and set
\[
 \mathcal E_T(c)=\mathcal H_T\cap\{\widehat q_T(c)\ge\omega_{c,T}/2\}.
\]
Define the total early-scale event-truncated sandwich by
\[
 \widehat V_T(c)=
 \begin{cases}
 \widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top},
   &\text{on }\mathcal E_T(c),\\
 I_d,&\text{on }\mathcal E_T(c)^c.
 \end{cases}
\]
Thus every inverse is evaluated only on \(\mathcal H_T\), and \(c^\top\widehat V_T(c)c>0\) for every realization because \(c\ne0\).

definitions.name: contrast-specific early-scale realized-QV Wald pivot
definitions.construction:
For the prespecified nonzero \(c\), use the early-scale event-truncated sandwich \(\widehat V_T(c)\) and define the everywhere finite statistic
\[
 T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)=
 \frac{\sqrt T\,c^\top(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)}
 {\sqrt{c^\top\widehat V_T(c)c}}.
\]
The denominator is positive on every realization by the construction of \(\widehat V_T(c)\).

definitions.name: bounded-noise Guo--Xu no-intercept recursion
definitions.construction: Fix \(K=2\), draw \(X_t\) independently and uniformly from \(\{-4,1\}\), and set \(Y_t(1)=1/2+\sigma_1R_{t,1}\) and \(Y_t(2)=1/12+\sigma_2R_{t,2}\), where the \(R_{t,a}\) are independent centered Rademacher innovations and \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2>0\) are arbitrary fixed constants declared as part of this bounded analogue; no numerical innovation variances are attributed to Guo and Xu. Keep their no-intercept working model, ridge constant \(\lambda=1\), unit-precision ridge initialization, and updates \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_t^2\), \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_tY_t\), and \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}/\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\). For \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), initialize \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_0=\iota_{\mathrm{GX}}(\eta_0)=(\eta_{0,1},\eta_{0,2},1,1)^\top\), equivalently \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=1\) and \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=\eta_{0,a}\); the published initialization is the included case \(\eta_0=(0,0)^\top\). At occasion \(t\), break every exact index tie in favor of arm \(1\), maximize \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}X_t+|X_t|\sqrt{q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}}\), and then assign the maximizing arm with probability \(0.99\) and the other arm with probability \(0.01\). The process of interest is the slope projection \((\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\) of \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), not a slope-only Markov chain.

definitions.name: bounded-recursion dynamics certification handle
definitions.construction: Write \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t=(\beta_1,\beta_2,q_1,q_2)^\top\) for a current augmented state. Its induced armwise update is \(q_a^+=q_a/(1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2)\) and \(\beta_a^+=(\beta_a+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aXY(a))/(1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2)\). The next clipped-UCB action uses \(\beta_aX+|X|\sqrt{q_a}\), so \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), rather than its two-dimensional slope projection, is the time-homogeneous Markov state. For stochastic-approximation analysis, put \(D_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), \(N_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), and, for \(t\ge1\), \(\Psi_t=(D_{t,1}/t,D_{t,2}/t,N_{t,1}/t,N_{t,2}/t)\). Analyze the exact \(1/(t+1)\) recursion for \(\Psi_t\) on an eventually compact region with both normalized Gram coordinates bounded away from zero. At the equal-slope surface, retain every limiting conditional-mean mode generated by the square-root UCB bonus: although the bonus is \(O(t^{-1/2})\), it can make the same arm greedy at both contexts inside an \(O(t^{-1/2})\) switching layer. Thus a closed convexified limiting graph must include these same-arm modes as well as the two opposite-context modes. Any differential-inclusion reduction must verify the closed-graph, compact-convex-value, boundedness, vanishing-perturbation, and martingale-tail conditions for this normalized recursion. Compact-uniform sequences \(r_T(K_0),\delta_T(K_0)\to0\) require a separate quantitative hitting or escape estimate and may not be inferred from pointwise convergence by a finite-cover argument.

definitions.name: contrast-specific early-scale realized-QV Wald interval
definitions.construction:
For the prespecified nonzero \(c\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), use the early-scale event-truncated sandwich and define the total Wald interval
\[
 I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_T-z_{1-\alpha/2}
 \sqrt{c^\top\widehat V_T(c)c/T},\ 
 \widehat\tau_T+z_{1-\alpha/2}
 \sqrt{c^\top\widehat V_T(c)c/T}\right].
\]

definitions.name: early-stabilized projected adaptive IPW-Z class
definitions.construction:
Fix a prespecified \(c\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\), the common objects \(\varepsilon,B,D_1,D_2,h_-,\kappa,s_\Theta,\rho,\Theta\), deterministic tolerance sequences \((r_T,\delta_T)_{T\ge1}\), deterministic integers \(0\le k_T<T\), and deterministic numbers \(\omega_{c,T}>0\) satisfying
\[
 T\omega_{c,T}\longrightarrow\infty,
 \qquad
 \frac{k_T}{T\omega_{c,T}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Let \((\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c))_{T\ge1}\) be any chosen sequence of law classes such that every \(P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)\) satisfies
\[
 \mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}full\text{-}data},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:sequential\text{-}randomization},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}overlap},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}score},
\]
\[
 \mathrm{ass:smooth\text{-}z\text{-}map},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}root\text{-}separation},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:root\text{-}interior},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:jacobian\text{-}nonsingular},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:vanishing\text{-}modulus}.
\]
For each member law there must exist a positive random scale \(\Lambda_T\), measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_{k_T}\), such that \(\Lambda_T\ge\omega_{c,T}\) almost surely and the chosen class sequence satisfies \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}projected\text{-}predictable\text{-}qv\text{-}growth}\). No information-growth condition is imposed in a direction orthogonal to \(H^{-\top}c\), and neither finite attractors nor convergence of the full matrix \(T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T\) is required.

statements.statement:
The common derivative and bounded-IPW envelopes imply
\[
 \|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1,
 \qquad
 \omega_-I_d\preceq\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d
 \quad\text{for every }j\in\mathcal J=\{1,\ldots,m\}.
\]
The finite-tail-selection relation gives \(\Omega_\infty=\Omega_J\) and \(V_\infty=V_J\) almost surely. There is a finite constant \(C\), independent of \(T\) and \(P\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P\!\left[
 \left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right]
 \le C(r_T+\delta_T).
\]
The preliminary estimator is uniformly consistent, \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), and \(\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Together with \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\), these bounds imply that, with probability tending uniformly to one, there is a unique empirical root in the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), it is \(O_P(T^{-1/2})\) from \(\theta^*\), and it is the unique member of \(\mathcal Z_T\). Hence \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), and
\[
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(e_T)
\]
uniformly.

For every basin \(j\in\mathcal J\), the basin-conditional Gaussian approximation is uniform:
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\!\left\{c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\mid J=j\right\}
 -\Phi\!\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_jc}}\right)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
More strongly, the corresponding joint \(\sigma(J)\)-stable Gaussian kernel is expressed by
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \sup_{\psi:\{1,\ldots,m\}\to[-1,1]}
 \left|E_P\!\left[\psi(J)\mathbf1\!\left\{
 c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\right\}\right]
 -\sum_{j=1}^mp_j\psi(j)\Phi\!\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_jc}}\right)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac{\omega_-}{(KD_1)^2}I_d\preceq V_j
 \preceq\frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon h_-^2}I_d
 \quad\text{for every }j\in\mathcal J.
\]
Thus, for every sequence \(P_T\in\mathfrak P_T\), the laws of \(V_J\) have a weakly convergent subsequence with a limiting law \(\mu\) supported on the displayed compact covariance set. Along that subsequence, every fixed nonzero contrast has the centered Gaussian scale-mixture limit \(\sqrt{c^\top Vc}\,Z_1\), where \(V\sim\mu\), \(Z_1\sim N(0,1)\), and \(V\) and \(Z_1\) are independent. This limit is Gaussian if and only if \(c^\top Vc\) is \(\mu\)-almost surely constant. No pointwise convergence of \(\eta_t\) is used.
statements.justification: This theorem derives predictable-QV control, exact-root localization, basin-conditional Gaussian limits, and the joint sigma(J)-stable Gaussian kernel from separated finite attractors and one common Cesaro modulus.
statements.gap: Guo and Xu prove ordinary Gaussian inference after inverse propensities stabilize and display two numerical modes; they do not prove a uniform finite-attractor stable kernel. Their bounded diagnostic analogue has two separated lock-in events but also a continuum of switching-surface equilibria, so it does not certify this class.
statements.consumer: A HeartSteps-style online learner can retain the deployment-selected basin in the asymptotic law for a prespecified causal excursion contrast without assuming pointwise convergence of the adaptive state.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(g_{t,a}(\theta)=g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\).  By sequential randomization, conditional independence of the current action and potential outcomes, independent full-data arrivals, and \(M_P(\theta^*)=0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[\xi_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]
&=E_P\!\left[E_P\!\left\{\left.\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}g_{t,a}(\theta^*)}
 {\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})}
 \right|W_t,\mathcal F_{t-1}\right\}\middle|\mathcal F_{t-1}\right]\\
&=E_P\!\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}g_{t,a}(\theta^*)\right]
=M_P(\theta^*)=0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]
Thus \((\xi_t,\mathcal F_t)\) is a martingale-difference array.  The same calculation, now for the outer product, and \(\mathrm{def:basin\text{-}covariance}\) give
\[
 E_P[\xi_t\xi_t^\top\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]
 =\Gamma_P(\eta_{t-1}),\qquad \Omega_J=\Gamma_P(\bar\eta_J).
\tag{2}
\]
The bounded-score and overlap assumptions imply \(\|\xi_t\|_2\le B/\varepsilon\).  For every unit vector \(u\),
\[
 u^\top\Gamma_P(\eta)u
 \le E_P\!\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \frac{\|g_{t,a}(\theta^*)\|_2^2}{\Pi(a\mid X_t,\eta)}\right]
 \le \frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon}.
\tag{3}
\]
Hence \(\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d\).  Since \(P(J=j)\ge p_->0\), finite-tail selection and basin nondegeneracy imply \(\Omega_j\succeq\omega_-I_d\): otherwise this deterministic inequality would fail for \(\Omega_\infty=\Omega_J\) on the positive-probability event \(\{J=j\}\).  The derivative envelope permits differentiation under the finite sum and expectation, so
\[
 \|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le E_P\!\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \|\partial_\theta g_{t,a}(\theta^*)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right]
 \le KD_1.
\tag{4}
\]

For \(p,q\ge\varepsilon\), \(|p^{-1}-q^{-1}|\le |p-q|/\varepsilon^2\).  Policy Lipschitzness and the covariance definition therefore imply
\[
 \|\Gamma_P(\eta)-\Gamma_P(\eta')\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le L_\Gamma\|\eta-\eta'\|_2,qquad
 L_\Gamma=\frac{KB^2L_\Pi}{\varepsilon^2},
\tag{5}
\]
and \(\|\Gamma_P(\eta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le M_\Gamma:=KB^2/\varepsilon\).  On
\[
 \mathcal A_T=\left\{T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T
 \|\eta_{t-1}-\bar\eta_J\|_2\le r_T\right\},
\]
equations (2) and (5) give
\[
 \left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le L_\Gamma r_T.
\tag{6}
\]
On \(\mathcal A_T^c\) the norm is at most \(2M_\Gamma\), and uniform attraction gives \(P(\mathcal A_T^c)\le\delta_T\).  Consequently
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P\!\left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-
 \Omega_J\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le L_\Gamma r_T+2M_\Gamma\delta_T
 \le C(r_T+\delta_T),
\tag{7}
\]
where \(C=\max\{L_\Gamma,2M_\Gamma\}\) is independent of \(T\) and \(P\).

We next localize an exact root.  For fixed \(\theta\), the calculation in (1), with \(\theta^*\) replaced by \(\theta\), makes the summands of \(G_T(\theta)-M_P(\theta)\) bounded martingale differences.  Martingale orthogonality gives
\[
 E_P\|G_T(\theta)-M_P(\theta)\|_2^2\le C_0/T.
\tag{8}
\]
The empirical and population maps are uniformly Lipschitz in \(\theta\), with moduli \(D_1/\varepsilon\) and \(KD_1\).  A finite mesh of the fixed compact set \(\Theta\), Chebyshev's inequality applied to (8), and a union bound therefore yield, for every fixed \(x>0\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P\!\left\{\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}
 \|G_T(\theta)-M_P(\theta)\|_2>x\right\}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{9}
\]
The preliminary estimator inequality, \(M_P(\theta^*)=0\), and (9) imply
\[
 \|M_P(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2
 \le2\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)-M_P(\theta)\|_2
 +T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T)=o_P(1)
\tag{10}
\]
uniformly.  Root separation hence gives, for each \(u>0\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P\{\|\widetilde\theta_T-\theta^*\|_2\ge u\}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P\{\|M_P(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2
 \ge\kappa(u)\}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{11}
\]

At the root, \(G_T(\theta^*)=S_T/T\).  Equations (1) and (3) give \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly.  The same entrywise martingale-orthogonality argument for the bounded derivative score gives
\[
 R_T^H:=\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2}).
\tag{12}
\]
Throughout the closed \(\rho\)-ball, curvature and overlap give
\[
 \sup_{\|\theta-\theta^*\|_2\le\rho}
 \|\partial_\theta G_T(\theta)-H\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\|R_T^H\|_{\mathrm{op}}+D_2\rho/\varepsilon.
\tag{13}
\]
The radius restriction, (12), and \(\sigma_{\min}(H)\ge h_-\) make the right side smaller than \(h_-/2\) with probability tending uniformly to one.  On that event define \(\Psi_T(\theta)=\theta-H^{-1}G_T(\theta)\).  Then \(\Psi_T\) has contraction modulus at most \(1/2\), and
\[
 \|\Psi_T(\theta)-\theta^*\|_2
 \le\tfrac12\|\theta-\theta^*\|_2+h_-^{-1}\|G_T(\theta^*)\|_2.
\tag{14}
\]
With uniformly asymptotic probability one the last term is at most \(\rho/2\), while root interiority puts the entire ball in \(\Theta\).  Iteration from \(\theta^*\) stays in the ball and its successive increments decrease geometrically.  It therefore converges to a fixed point \(\theta_T^0\); closedness and continuity give existence, and the contraction inequality gives uniqueness in the ball.  Moreover,
\[
 \|\theta_T^0-\theta^*\|_2
 \le2h_-^{-1}\|G_T(\theta^*)\|_2=O_P(T^{-1/2}).
\tag{15}
\]
Equations (11) and (15) put both \(\widetilde\theta_T\) and \(\theta_T^0\) within \(\rho/4\) of \(\theta^*\) with probability tending uniformly to one.  Then \(\theta_T^0\in\mathcal Z_T\), while each member of \(\mathcal Z_T\) lies within \(3\rho/4\) of \(\theta^*\) and so equals \(\theta_T^0\).  Thus \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), and the selected estimator equals \(\theta_T^0\) outside a uniformly negligible event.

Put \(\Delta_T=\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*\).  On the exact-root event, Taylor's formula gives
\[
 0=T^{-1}S_T+H\Delta_T+R_T^H\Delta_T+R_T^{(2)},
 \qquad \|R_T^{(2)}\|_2\le\frac{D_2}{2\varepsilon}\|\Delta_T\|_2^2.
\tag{16}
\]
Using (12), (15), and \(\|H^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le h_-^{-1}\) in (16) yields
\[
 \sqrt T\Delta_T+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T
 =O_P(T^{-1/2})=O_P(e_T).
\tag{17}
\]
The fallback event is uniformly negligible, so (17) holds unconditionally in the uniform-in-probability sense.

It remains to prove the basin kernel.  Set
\[
 \beta_T=\max\{T^{-1/2},\sqrt{r_T}\},\qquad
 k_T=\min\{T-1,\lceil T\beta_T\rceil\}.
\tag{18}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(T\), \(1\le k_T<T\), and the vanishing modulus gives
\[
 \frac{k_T}{T}\longrightarrow0,qquad
 \frac{Tr_T}{k_T}\le\frac{r_T}{\beta_T}
 \le\sqrt{r_T}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{19}
\]
Let \(J_T\) be the fixed-tie-broken nearest attractor to \(k_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{k_T}\eta_{t-1}\).  It is \(\mathcal F_{k_T}\)-measurable.  On \(\mathcal A_T\),
\[
 \left\|k_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{k_T}\eta_{t-1}-\bar\eta_J\right\|_2
 \le\frac{Tr_T}{k_T}.
\tag{20}
\]
If \(m=1\), then \(J_T=J=1\).  If \(m\ge2\), the right side of (20) is eventually smaller than \(s_\eta/2\), so attractor separation makes \(\bar\eta_J\) uniquely nearest.  Hence
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(J_T\ne J)\le\delta_T\longrightarrow0,
\tag{21}
\]
and the mass floor gives \(P(J_T=j)\ge p_-/2\) uniformly for large \(T\).

Fix a unit vector \(c\), put \(a=H^{-\top}c\), and define \(X_t=-a^\top\xi_t\).  Equations (3)--(4) and Jacobian nonsingularity imply
\[
 \frac1{KD_1}\le\|a\|_2\le\frac1{h_-},
 \qquad |X_t|\le L:=\frac{B}{\varepsilon h_-}.
\tag{22}
\]
For \(\lambda_j=a^\top\Omega_ja=c^\top V_jc\),
\[
 v_0:=\frac{\omega_-}{(KD_1)^2}\le\lambda_j
 \le v_1:=\frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon h_-^2}.
\tag{23}
\]
On \(\mathcal A_T\cap\{J_T=j\}\), equations (5), (19), and (20) give
\[
 \left\|T^{-1}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^T\Gamma_P(\eta_{t-1})-
 \Omega_j\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le L_\Gamma r_T+M_\Gamma k_T/T.
\tag{24}
\]
The left side is always at most \(2M_\Gamma\).  Restricting to \(\{J_T=j\}\), taking expectations, dividing by \(P(J_T=j)\ge p_-/2\), and using \(P(\mathcal A_T^c)\le\delta_T\), equations (2) and (24) imply
\[
 E_P\!\left[\left.\left|T^{-1}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^T
 E_P[X_t^2\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]-\lambda_j\right|
 \right|J_T=j\right]
 \le C\{r_T+k_T/T+\delta_T\}\longrightarrow0
\tag{25}
\]
uniformly in \(P,c,j\).

Because \(\{J_T=j\}\in\mathcal F_{k_T}\), conditioning on it preserves the martingale-difference property for every \(t>k_T\).  Apply \(\mathrm{lem:early\text{-}measurable\text{-}martingale\text{-}mixture}\) under \(P(\,\cdot\mid J_T=j)\), using the constant scale \(\lambda_j\), the bound (22), the scale bounds (23), and (25).  We obtain
\[
 \sup_{P,c,j,z}\left|P\!\left\{T^{-1/2}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^TX_t\le z
 \mid J_T=j\right\}
 -\Phi\!\left(\frac z{\sqrt{\lambda_j}}\right)\right|\longrightarrow0,
\tag{26}
\]
where \(c\) ranges over the unit sphere.  Unconditional martingale orthogonality, (22), and \(P(J_T=j)\ge p_-/2\) give
\[
 E_P\!\left[\left.\left|T^{-1/2}\sum_{t=1}^{k_T}X_t\right|^2
 \right|J_T=j\right]
 \le\frac{2L^2k_T}{p_-T}=o(1).
\tag{27}
\]
The remainder in (17) is uniformly \(o_P(1)\); conditioning on \(\{J_T=j\}\) preserves this because those events have probability at least \(p_-/2\).  For arbitrary \(Y,R\) and \(h>0\),
\[
 P(Y\le z-h)-P(|R|>h)\le P(Y+R\le z)
 \le P(Y\le z+h)+P(|R|>h).
\tag{28}
\]
The Gaussian densities in (26) are bounded uniformly by \((2\pi v_0)^{-1/2}\).  Applying (28), first letting \(T\to\infty\) and then \(h\downarrow0\), transfers (26) across the prefix and linearization remainder.  Finally, for every event \(D\),
\[
 \left|P(D\mid J=j)-P(D\mid J_T=j)\right|
 \le\frac{2P(J_T\ne J)}{\min\{P(J=j),P(J_T=j)\}}
 \le\frac{4\delta_T}{p_-}.
\tag{29}
\]
Thus (21) and (26)--(29) prove the asserted basin-conditional approximation without conditioning a martingale on the terminal event \(\{J=j\}\).

For every \(\psi:\{1,\ldots,m\}\to[-1,1]\), decompose over the basin events:
\[
 E_P[\psi(J)\mathbf1\{Z_T\le z\}]
 =\sum_{j=1}^mp_j\psi(j)P(Z_T\le z\mid J=j),
 \quad Z_T=c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*).
\tag{30}
\]
The difference from the Gaussian-kernel sum is bounded by the largest conditional Kolmogorov error because \(\sum_jp_j|\psi(j)|\le1\).  This proves the joint \(\sigma(J)\)-stable formula.  Equation (23), for every unit \(c\), is equivalent to
\[
 \frac{\omega_-}{(KD_1)^2}I_d\preceq V_j
 \preceq\frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon h_-^2}I_d.
\tag{31}
\]
Terminal selection also gives \(\Omega_\infty=\Omega_J\) and \(V_\infty=V_J\) almost surely.

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:compact\text{-}covariance\text{-}law\text{-}subsequence}\) to (31).  Along the resulting subsequence, take \(\psi\equiv1\) in (30).  The map \(v\mapsto\Phi(z/\sqrt{c^\top vc})\) is continuous on the compact covariance set, so weak convergence of the laws of \(V_J\) gives the limit \(\sqrt{c^\top Vc}\,Z_1\), with \(V\sim\mu\) independent of \(Z_1\sim N(0,1)\).  If \(c^\top Vc=q_0\) almost surely, this is \(N(0,q_0)\).  Conversely, if it is \(N(0,\sigma^2)\), compact support permits comparison of second and fourth moments.  Direct Gaussian integration gives \(E[Z_1^2]=1\) and \(E[Z_1^4]=3\), whence
\[
 E[c^\top Vc]=\sigma^2,
 \qquad E[(c^\top Vc)^2]=\sigma^4.
\tag{32}
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{Var}(c^\top Vc)=0\).  This proves the Gaussian characterization.  The only state approximation used was the Cesaro bound (20), never pointwise convergence of \(\eta_t\).

statements.statement:
Fix a prespecified \(c\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\). For the early-stabilized projected class \(\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)\), the exact-root event is uniformly asymptotically certain and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P(E_T^c)\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T
 =O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly. Moreover,
\[
 T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat\Omega_T-T^{-1}[S]_T=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat H_T-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly over that class. Although no information growth is required outside the direction \(H^{-\top}c\), the early-scale condition with \(T\omega_{c,T}\to\infty\) makes the contrast-specific truncation inactive:
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P\{\mathcal E_T(c)^c\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|
 \longrightarrow0,
\]
and, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}
 \left|P\{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Every finite-tail-attractor class \(\mathfrak P_T\) satisfies this early-stabilized condition for each fixed nonzero \(c\). At every horizon set
\[
 k_T=\min\!\left\{T-1,\left\lceil T\max\{T^{-1/2},\sqrt{r_T}\}\right\rceil\right\}.
\]
For \(k_T\ge1\), let \(J_T\) be the nearest attractor to \(k_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{k_T}\eta_{t-1}\), with fixed tie-breaking, and set \(J_T=1\) when \(k_T=0\). With \(a=H^{-\top}c\), take
\[
 \Lambda_T=a^\top\Omega_{J_T}a,\qquad
 \omega_{c,T}=\frac{\omega_-\|c\|_2^2}{(KD_1)^2}.
\]
Then \(J_T\) and \(\Lambda_T\) are \(\mathcal F_{k_T}\)-measurable, all early-scale conditions hold uniformly, and the same pivot and coverage conclusions follow.
statements.justification: An early-measurable directional information scale, a negligible prefix, bounded adaptive IPW scores, and \(T\omega_{c,T}\to\infty\) suffice for a total realized-QV pivot and uniform Wald coverage; the exact bounded Saco specialization shows that predictable-QV lower growth alone does not.
statements.gap: Saco, arXiv:2602.15559v1, Theorem 5.14, asserts a variance-growth-only Studentized central limit theorem. The bounded AIPW specialization in the counterexample proposition satisfies the published hypotheses and refutes that conclusion. This theorem supplies the missing early-measurability boundary, proves uniform exact-root localization and feasible square-root QV comparison, and makes truncation asymptotically inactive.
statements.consumer: For a HeartSteps-style causal excursion contrast fixed before analysis, inference remains valid when irrelevant score directions are weak, provided the target-direction suffix scale is early measurable and the prefix is negligible.
statements.proof_tex:
All stochastic orders below are uniform over \(P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)\).  Fix the prespecified \(c\ne0\), and put
\[
 Z_t(\theta)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \frac{\mathbf1\{A_t=a\}g(a,X_t,Y_t;\theta)}
 {\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})},
 \qquad G_T(\theta)=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^TZ_t(\theta).
\tag{1}
\]
Sequential randomization and independent full-data arrivals give
\[
 E_P[Z_t(\theta)\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]
 =E_P\!\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\right]
 =M_P(\theta).
\tag{2}
\]
At \(\theta^*\), \(Z_t(\theta^*)=\xi_t\) is a martingale difference and \(G_T(\theta^*)=S_T/T\).  Bounded scores and overlap imply
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\|Z_t(\theta)\|_2\le M_0:=B/\varepsilon,
 \qquad E_P\|G_T(\theta^*)\|_2^2\le M_0^2/T.
\tag{3}
\]

For root localization, the derivative envelope makes \(G_T\) and \(M_P\) Lipschitz in \(\theta\), with common moduli \(D_1/\varepsilon\) and \(KD_1\).  For fixed \(u>0\), take a finite net of the common compact set \(\Theta\) with mesh smaller than
\[
 \frac{\kappa(u)}{8(D_1/\varepsilon+KD_1)}.
\tag{4}
\]
At each net point the centered terms in (2) are martingale differences of norm at most \(2M_0\), so
\[
 E_P\|G_T(\theta)-M_P(\theta)\|_2^2\le4M_0^2/T.
\tag{5}
\]
Chebyshev's inequality, a finite union bound, and the Lipschitz bounds yield
\[
 \sup_P P\!\left\{\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}
 \|G_T(\theta)-M_P(\theta)\|_2>\kappa(u)/2\right\}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{6}
\]
The preliminary estimator inequality and (3) give
\[
 \|G_T(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2
 \le\|G_T(\theta^*)\|_2+T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T)=o_P(1).
\tag{7}
\]
Equations (6)--(7) and root separation prove \(\widetilde\theta_T\to\theta^*\) uniformly in probability.

Let \(A_T^\partial=\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)\).  Differentiating (2) under the common derivative envelope makes every entry of \(A_T^\partial-H\) an average of bounded matrix martingale differences.  Since \(d\) is fixed,
\[
 A_T^\partial-H=O_P(T^{-1/2}).
\tag{8}
\]
The Jacobian lower bound and the singular-value perturbation inequality imply, with probability tending uniformly to one,
\[
 \sigma_{\min}(A_T^\partial)\ge h_-/2,
 \qquad \|(A_T^\partial)^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2/h_-.
\tag{9}
\]
For \(\|\theta-\theta^*\|_2\le\rho\), curvature and overlap give
\[
 \|\partial_\theta G_T(\theta)-A_T^\partial\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le(D_2/\varepsilon)\|\theta-\theta^*\|_2.
\tag{10}
\]
On (9), \(F_T(\theta)=\theta-(A_T^\partial)^{-1}G_T(\theta)\) has Lipschitz modulus at most
\[
 q_0=\frac{2D_2\rho}{\varepsilon h_-}<\frac12
\tag{11}
\]
on the closed \(\rho\)-ball.  Root interiority puts this ball in \(\Theta\), and (3), (9) make \(\|F_T(\theta^*)-\theta^*\|_2=O_P(T^{-1/2})\).  Thus, with uniformly asymptotic probability one, \(F_T\) maps the ball into itself.  Its iterates are Cauchy by (11), so closedness and continuity give a unique fixed point \(\theta_T^0\), with
\[
 \|\theta_T^0-\theta^*\|_2
 \le\frac{\|(A_T^\partial)^{-1}G_T(\theta^*)\|_2}{1-q_0}
 =O_P(T^{-1/2}).
\tag{12}
\]
Consistency of \(\widetilde\theta_T\) and (12) place this root within \(\rho/2\) of \(\widetilde\theta_T\), while every member of \(\mathcal Z_T\) lies in the \(\rho\)-ball.  Uniqueness therefore gives
\[
 \sup_P P(E_T^c)\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad \widehat\theta_T-\theta^*=O_P(T^{-1/2}).
\tag{13}
\]
On \(E_T\), the fundamental theorem of calculus gives
\[
 0=G_T(\widehat\theta_T)=G_T(\theta^*)+\overline H_T
 (\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*),
 \quad
 \overline H_T=\int_0^1\partial_\theta G_T
 (\theta^*+s(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*))\,ds.
\tag{14}
\]
Equations (8), (10), and (13) imply \(\overline H_T-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})\).  The inverse identity
\[
 \overline H_T^{-1}-H^{-1}
 =\overline H_T^{-1}(H-\overline H_T)H^{-1}
\tag{15}
\]
and (3), (14) yield
\[
 R_T:=\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)
 +H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(T^{-1/2}).
\tag{16}
\]
The fallback branch changes only the uniformly negligible event \(E_T^c\).

For the matrix comparisons, define
\[
 D_t=\xi_t\xi_t^\top-E_P[\xi_t\xi_t^\top\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}].
\tag{17}
\]
Every entry is a martingale difference and \(\|D_t\|_{\mathrm F}\le2M_0^2\).  Entrywise orthogonality gives
\[
 E_P\left\|T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^TD_t\right\|_{\mathrm F}^2
 \le C_dM_0^4/T.
\tag{18}
\]
Thus \(T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\).  Smoothness, overlap, and (13) give
\[
 \|\widehat\xi_t-\xi_t\|_2
 \le(D_1/\varepsilon)\|\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*\|_2.
\tag{19}
\]
Expanding the score outer-product difference and using boundedness gives
\[
 \widehat\Omega_T-T^{-1}[S]_T=O_P(T^{-1/2}),
 \qquad \widehat H_T-H=O_P(T^{-1/2}).
\tag{20}
\]

For the directional step put
\[
 a=H^{-\top}c,\qquad U_t=a^\top\xi_t,\qquad
 Q_T^c=\sum_{t=1}^TU_t^2=a^\top[S]_Ta.
\tag{21}
\]
Jacobian nonsingularity and (3) give
\[
 |U_t|\le L_c:=\frac{B\|c\|_2}{\varepsilon h_-}.
\tag{22}
\]
The class definition supplies a positive \(\mathcal F_{k_T}\)-measurable \(\Lambda_T\ge\omega_{c,T}\) such that
\[
 T\omega_{c,T}\longrightarrow\infty,
 \qquad \frac{k_T}{T\omega_{c,T}}\longrightarrow0,
\tag{23}
\]
and projected predictable-QV growth says
\[
 \frac{\sum_{t=k_T+1}^TE_P[U_t^2\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]}
 {T\Lambda_T}\longrightarrow1
\tag{24}
\]
uniformly in probability.  Apply \(\mathrm{lem:early\text{-}measurable\text{-}scale\text{-}self\text{-}normalized\text{-}martingale\text{-}clt}\) with \(N_n=T\), \(h_n=k_T\), \(\lambda_n=\Lambda_T\), and \(\nu_n=\omega_{c,T}\).  Equations (22)--(24) verify all its hypotheses, so
\[
 \frac{Q_T^c}{T\Lambda_T}\longrightarrow1,
 \qquad \frac{a^\top S_T}{\sqrt{Q_T^c}}\Rightarrow N(0,1)
\tag{25}
\]
uniformly.  Uniform weak convergence to the continuous standard-normal law is equivalent here to uniform Kolmogorov convergence: on a compact interval use a finite grid and monotonicity, and then use the normal tails outside that interval.

Equation (20), the Jacobian lower bound, and (15) imply \(P(\mathcal H_T^c)\to0\) and, on \(\mathcal H_T\),
\[
 \|\widehat H_T^{-1}-H^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(T^{-1/2}).
\tag{26}
\]
Let
\[
 q_T^0=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T(a^\top\xi_t)^2,\qquad
 \widehat u_t=c^\top\widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\xi_t
 \quad\text{on }\mathcal H_T.
\tag{27}
\]
The reverse triangle inequality in Euclidean \(T\)-space, followed by (19), (26), \(\|\widehat\xi_t\|_2\le M_0\), and \(\|a\|_2\le\|c\|_2/h_-\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \left|\sqrt{\widehat q_T(c)}-\sqrt{q_T^0}\right|
 &\le\left\{T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T
 |\widehat u_t-a^\top\xi_t|^2\right\}^{1/2}\\
 &\le \|c\|_2\|\widehat H_T^{-1}-H^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}M_0
 +\|a\|_2(D_1/\varepsilon)\|\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*\|_2\\
 &=O_P(T^{-1/2}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{28}
\]
Division by \(\sqrt{\Lambda_T}\ge\sqrt{\omega_{c,T}}\) is legal, and (23) makes the resulting error \(o_P(1)\).  Combining (25) and (28) yields, on \(\mathcal H_T\),
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{\widehat q_T(c)}}{\sqrt{\Lambda_T}}=1+o_P(1).
\tag{29}
\]
Therefore \(\widehat q_T(c)\ge\Lambda_T/2\ge\omega_{c,T}/2\) with probability tending uniformly to one, so
\[
 \sup_P P\{\mathcal E_T(c)^c\}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{30}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_T(c)\), (16), (23), and (29) imply
\[
 \frac{|c^\top R_T|}{\sqrt{\widehat q_T(c)}}
 =O_P\!\left(\frac1{\sqrt{T\omega_{c,T}}}\right)=o_P(1).
\tag{31}
\]
Using (16), (21), (25), and (29) in the pivot definition gives
\[
 T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)
 =-\frac{a^\top S_T}{\sqrt{Q_T^c}}+o_P(1).
\tag{32}
\]
The complement of \(\mathcal E_T(c)\) is negligible by (30).  For any \(h>0\), the inclusions
\[
 \{Y_T\le z-h\}\setminus\{|R_T'|>h\}
 \subseteq\{Y_T+R_T'\le z\}
 \subseteq\{Y_T\le z+h\}\cup\{|R_T'|>h\}
\tag{33}
\]
together with (25), uniform continuity of \(\Phi\), and then \(h\downarrow0\), prove the uniform Kolmogorov limit.  Since \(\tau=c^\top\theta^*\),
\[
 \{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}
 =\{|T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)|\le z_{1-\alpha/2}\}.
\tag{34}
\]
The normal limit and \(2\Phi(z_{1-\alpha/2})-1=1-\alpha\) prove coverage.

Finally take \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\).  Set
\[
 \beta_T=\max\{T^{-1/2},\sqrt{r_T}\},\qquad
 k_T=\min\{T-1,\lceil T\beta_T\rceil\}.
\tag{35}
\]
This gives \(0\le k_T<T\) at every horizon.  Since \(r_T\to0\), it also gives \(k_T/T\to0\), and eventually \(k_T=\lceil T\beta_T\rceil\ge1\) with \(Tr_T/k_T\le r_T/\beta_T\to0\).  Let \(J_T\) be the fixed-tie-broken nearest attractor to \(k_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{k_T}\eta_{t-1}\), using its declared value \(1\) when \(k_T=0\).  Then \(J_T\) is \(\mathcal F_{k_T}\)-measurable.  On the attraction event,
\[
 \left\|k_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{k_T}\eta_{t-1}-\bar\eta_J\right\|_2
 \le Tr_T/k_T<s_\eta/2
\tag{36}
\]
eventually.  Separation gives \(J_T=J\) there, hence \(\sup_PP(J_T\ne J)\le\delta_T\to0\).

With \(a=H^{-\top}c\), take
\[
 \Lambda_T=a^\top\Omega_{J_T}a,\qquad
 \omega_{c,T}=\frac{\omega_-\|c\|_2^2}{(KD_1)^2}.
\tag{37}
\]
The scale is \(\mathcal F_{k_T}\)-measurable.  The basin-stable theorem gives \(\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1\) and \(\Omega_j\succeq\omega_-I_d\), whence
\[
 \Lambda_T\ge\omega_{c,T}>0.
\tag{38}
\]
The lower bound in (37) is constant in \(T\), so \(T\omega_{c,T}\to\infty\) and \(k_T/(T\omega_{c,T})\to0\).

Policy Lipschitzness, overlap, and bounded scores imply
\[
 \|\Gamma_P(\eta)-\Gamma_P(\eta')\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\frac{KB^2L_\Pi}{\varepsilon^2}\|\eta-\eta'\|_2,
 \qquad \|\Gamma_P(\eta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon}.
\tag{39}
\]
On the attraction event, where \(J_T=J\),
\[
 \left\|T^{-1}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^T\Gamma_P(\eta_{t-1})-
 \Omega_{J_T}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\frac{KB^2L_\Pi}{\varepsilon^2}r_T
 +\frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon}\frac{k_T}{T}.
\tag{40}
\]
Sequential randomization and independent full-data arrivals give
\[
 E_P[\xi_t\xi_t^\top\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]
 =\Gamma_P(\eta_{t-1}).
\tag{41}
\]
Since \(\|a\|_2\le\|c\|_2/h_-\) and the denominator in (37) is bounded below by (38), equations (39)--(41) yield on that event
\[
 \left|
 \frac{\sum_{t=k_T+1}^TE_P[(a^\top\xi_t)^2\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]}
 {T\Lambda_T}-1\right|
 \le C_c\left(r_T+\frac{k_T}{T}\right)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{42}
\]
The complementary probability is at most \(\delta_T\to0\) uniformly.  Thus (35)--(42) verify the relative suffix predictable-QV condition and all other early-scale premises.  The finite-attractor class inherits the pivot and coverage conclusions.

statements.statement:
Let \(T_\ell\to\infty\) and \(P_\ell\in\mathfrak P_{T_\ell}\) be a sequence along which the law of \(V_\infty\) under \(P_\ell\) converges weakly to a probability law \(\mu\) on the compact covariance set in Theorem 1. Let \(V\sim\mu\). Fix nonzero \(c\) and deterministic positive-definite \(\Sigma\). Then
\[
 \lim_{\ell\to\infty}P_\ell\{\tau\in C_{T_\ell}^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}=1-\alpha
 \quad\text{for every }\alpha\in(0,1)
\]
if and only if
\[
 c^\top Vc=c^\top\Sigma c\qquad\mu\text{-almost surely}.
\]
The necessity identifies the projected variance law of a general centered Gaussian scale mixture from coverage at every nominal level; it makes no claim from validity at only one level.
statements.justification: This theorem exactly characterizes every-level fixed-sandwich validity for one causal contrast under an arbitrary limiting covariance mixing law.
statements.gap: Directional-stability work gives sufficient target-specific conditions and Saco highlights random predictable variance; neither gives the general scale-mixture every-level converse.
statements.consumer: Trial analysts can decide whether a deterministic variance report remains valid for one prespecified HeartSteps excursion-effect contrast even when other covariance directions remain random.
statements.proof_tex:
Set \(s=c^\top\Sigma c>0\) and \(q(v)=c^\top vc\).  Positive definiteness of \(\Sigma\), the compact covariance lower bound in \(\mathrm{thm:basin\text{-}stable\text{-}ipwz}\), and \(c\ne0\) justify every square root and division below.  The interval definition gives
\[
 \{\tau\in C_{T_\ell}^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}
 =\left\{\left|\sqrt{T_\ell}\,c^\top
 (\widehat\theta_{T_\ell}-\theta^*)\right|
 \le z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt s\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Apply the basin-stable theorem to \(c/\|c\|_2\) and rescale.  Its marginal case \(\psi\equiv1\), evaluated at the positive and negative endpoints, gives for each fixed \(z>0\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &P_\ell\!\left\{\left|\sqrt{T_\ell}\,c^\top
 (\widehat\theta_{T_\ell}-\theta^*)\right|\le z\sqrt s\right\}\\
 &\quad=E_{P_\ell}\!\left[
 2\Phi\!\left(z\sqrt{\frac{s}{c^\top V_Jc}}\right)-1\right]+o(1).
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
The map \(v\mapsto2\Phi(z\sqrt{s/q(v)})-1\) is bounded and continuous on the compact covariance set.  Since \(V_J=V_\infty\) almost surely, weak convergence of the laws of \(V_\infty\) turns (2) into
\[
 \int\left\{2\Phi\!\left(z\sqrt{\frac{s}{q(v)}}\right)-1\right\}
 \,d\mu(v).
\tag{3}
\]
If \(q(V)=s\) \(\mu\)-almost surely, (3) equals \(2\Phi(z)-1\).  Taking \(z=z_{1-\alpha/2}\) proves sufficiency for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).

Conversely, suppose the coverage limit equals \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).  As \(\alpha\) ranges over this interval, \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\) ranges over \((0,\infty)\).  Equations (1)--(3) imply
\[
 \int\left\{2\Phi\!\left(z\sqrt{\frac{s}{q(v)}}\right)-1\right\}
 \,d\mu(v)=2\Phi(z)-1\qquad(z>0).
\tag{4}
\]
Let \(Q=q(V)\), let \(Z_1\sim N(0,1)\) be independent of \(V\), and set \(X=\sqrt QZ_1\).  Both \(X/\sqrt s\) and \(Z_1\) have continuous symmetric laws.  Equation (4) equates their absolute-value distribution functions at every positive argument, so symmetry equates their full laws.  The compact covariance bounds make \(Q\) bounded, and equality of laws permits comparison of second and fourth moments.  Direct Gaussian integration gives \(E[Z_1^2]=1\) and \(E[Z_1^4]=3\), whence
\[
 E[X^2]=E[Q]=s,
 \qquad E[X^4]=3E[Q^2]=3s^2.
\tag{5}
\]
Consequently
\[
 E[(Q-s)^2]=E[Q^2]-2sE[Q]+s^2=0.
\tag{6}
\]
Thus \(Q=s\) \(\mu\)-almost surely, proving necessity.  The argument uses all positive critical values through (4) and makes no inference from one isolated nominal level.

statements.statement:
Along any sequence for which the law of \(V_\infty\) converges weakly to \(\mu\), as in Theorem 3, one deterministic positive-definite matrix \(\Sigma\) gives asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and every nonzero contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^d\) if and only if
\[
 V=\Sigma\qquad\mu\text{-almost surely},
\]
where \(V\sim\mu\). Equivalently, the limiting covariance law is the point mass at \(\Sigma\). For a fixed law and horizon-asymptotic sequence, this specializes to \(V_\infty=\Sigma\) almost surely whenever the law of \(V_\infty\) itself is constant across horizons. The implication from all projected equalities to matrix equality uses only finitely many coordinate and pairwise-sum contrasts.
statements.justification: This theorem separates target-specific validity from target-agnostic covariance invariance for an arbitrary limiting covariance law.
statements.gap: Shen and coauthors distinguish directional from matrix stability on the sufficiency side; the general every-level necessity and finite-contrast polarization certificate remain unstated.
statements.consumer: Software reporting many adaptive-experiment contrasts can determine whether one fixed covariance matrix is defensible.
statements.proof_tex:
Suppose first that one deterministic positive-definite \(\Sigma\) gives the asserted coverage for every nonzero contrast and every nominal level.  Apply \(\mathrm{thm:contrastwise\text{-}deterministic\text{-}sandwich\text{-}iff}\) to the finite set
\[
 \mathcal C_0=\{e_r:1\le r\le d\}\cup
 \{e_r+e_s:1\le r<s\le d\}.
\tag{1}
\]
For each \(c\in\mathcal C_0\),
\[
 c^\top(V-\Sigma)c=0\qquad\mu\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{2}
\]
The intersection of these finitely many probability-one events still has probability one.  On it put \(A=V-\Sigma\), which is symmetric.  Taking \(c=e_r\) gives \(A_{rr}=0\).  For \(r<s\), taking \(c=e_r+e_s\) gives
\[
 0=(e_r+e_s)^\top A(e_r+e_s)=2A_{rs}.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus every entry of \(A\) vanishes and \(V=\Sigma\) almost surely.

Conversely, if \(V=\Sigma\) \(\mu\)-almost surely, then \(c^\top Vc=c^\top\Sigma c\) almost surely for every nonzero \(c\).  The contrastwise theorem gives coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every such contrast and every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).  This also proves the point-mass formulation.  If the law of \(V_\infty\) is constant across horizons along a fixed horizon-asymptotic sequence, that law is its own weak limit; hence the point-mass condition is exactly \(V_\infty=\Sigma\) almost surely.

statements.statement: For every \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/6)\), the bounded witness \(P^{\dagger}\) belongs at every \(T\ge2\) to a class \(\mathfrak P_T\) with common choices \(B=2\), \(D_1=D_2=1\), \(h_-=1\), \(L_\Pi=1/12\), \(\omega_-=1\), \(\kappa(u)=u\), \(s_\Theta=1\), \(\rho=\varepsilon/8\), \(r_T=1/(2T)\), and \(\delta_T=0\). Specifically, the policy floor is \(1/6\), \(\sup_{a,\theta}\|g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\|_2<2\), the derivative and curvature bounds are \(1\) and \(0\), \(M_{P^{\dagger}}(\theta)=-\theta\), every empirical moment admits an exact minimum of zero in \(\Theta\), and \(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\|\eta_{t-1}-\bar\eta_J\|_2=1/(2T)\) almost surely. Moreover, \(P^{\dagger}(J=1)=2/5\), \(P^{\dagger}(J=2)=3/5\), so \(\mathcal J=\{1,2\}\); tail selection is exact after the first assignment, \(H=-I_2\), \(\Omega_1=V_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\), and \(\Omega_2=V_2=\operatorname{diag}(1,3)\). Hence for \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\) and \(c=(1,0)^\top\), \(c^\top V_jc=c^\top\Sigma c=1\) in both positive-mass basins although \(V_1\ne V_2\), so contrastwise deterministic-sandwich validity holds while matrixwise invariance fails.
statements.justification: This elementary bounded construction verifies inside the stated law class that the contrastwise and matrixwise frontiers are logically distinct.
statements.gap: This is a non-novel existence witness, not evidence about the Guo--Xu recursion; its role is to prevent the directional and matrix claims from being conflated by an unattained free-matrix example.
statements.consumer: Applied analysts can retain a valid primary-endpoint interval in a concrete adaptive experiment without claiming that all secondary contrasts share a stable covariance.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/6)\), \(T\ge2\), and the law \(P^\dagger\) in \(\mathrm{def:directional\text{-}matrix\text{-}witness}\).  The context is constant and the displayed potential outcomes are independent across occasions, so the full-data vectors are independent and identically distributed.  At time \(t\), \(\eta_{t-1}\) is \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable and \(A_t\) is drawn from the declared policy independently of current potential outcomes, verifying sequential randomization.

Writing \(u\in[0,1]\) for the state, linear interpolation gives
\[
 \Pi(1\mid x,u)=\frac25,\qquad
 \Pi(2\mid x,u)=\frac14-\frac{u}{12},\qquad
 \Pi(3\mid x,u)=\frac7{20}+\frac{u}{12}.
\tag{1}
\]
The probabilities sum to one and their coordinatewise minimum is \(1/6>\varepsilon\).  Moreover,
\[
 \sup_{a\in\{1,2,3\}}|\Pi(a\mid x,u)-\Pi(a\mid x,u')|
 \le\frac1{12}|u-u'|,
\tag{2}
\]
so \(L_\Pi=1/12\) is valid.

For every \(\theta\in[-1,1]^2\),
\[
 |Y_t(1)-\theta_1|\le1+\sqrt{2/5}<2,
 \qquad |Y_t(2)-\theta_2|\le1+\sqrt{1/2}<2.
\tag{3}
\]
Each nonzero score has one nonzero coordinate and the third-arm score is zero, so \(B=2\) is a common envelope.  The scores are affine in \(\theta\), their derivative matrices are
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 \begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad 0,
\]
and all second derivatives vanish.  Hence \(D_1=D_2=1\) are valid envelopes.

Both nonzero outcomes have mean zero.  Therefore
\[
 M_{P^\dagger}(\theta)=(-\theta_1,-\theta_2)^\top=-\theta,
 \qquad H=-I_2.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus \(\theta^*=0\) is the unique root, \(\|M_{P^\dagger}(\theta)\|_2=\|\theta\|_2\), and \(\sigma_{\min}(H)=1\).  Hence \(\kappa(u)=u\), \(h_-=1\), and
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial[-1,1]^2)=1
\tag{5}
\]
gives \(s_\Theta=1\).

Every realized empirical moment has an exact zero in \(\Theta\).  For \(a\in\{1,2\}\), put
\[
 W_a=\sum_{t=1}^T\frac{\mathbf1\{A_t=a\}}
 {\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})}.
\]
If \(W_a>0\), define
\[
 \theta_a^{(0)}=
 \frac{\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf1\{A_t=a\}Y_t(a)/
 \pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})}{W_a};
\tag{6}
\]
if \(W_a=0\), set \(\theta_a^{(0)}=0\).  In the first case (6) is a convex combination of outcomes in \([-1,1]\); in the second the corresponding empirical coordinate is identically zero.  Hence \(\theta^{(0)}\in\Theta\), direct substitution gives \(G_T(\theta^{(0)})=0\), and
\[
 \min_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)\|_2=0.
\tag{7}
\]

At the first occasion \(\eta_0=1/2\), so (1) gives \(P^\dagger(A_1=1)=2/5\).  By the definition of \(J\),
\[
 P^\dagger(J=1)=\frac25,
 \qquad P^\dagger(J=2)=\frac35.
\tag{8}
\]
The label is \(\mathcal F_1\)-measurable, \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J\), and the fixed attractors are separated by one.  Thus tail selection holds with \(m=2\), separation with \(s_\eta=1\), and the basin-mass floor with \(p_-=2/5\).  Since \(\eta_s=\bar\eta_J\) for \(s\ge1\) and \(|\eta_0-\bar\eta_J|=1/2\),
\[
 \frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T|\eta_{t-1}-\bar\eta_J|=\frac1{2T}
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{9}
\]
The attraction condition holds with \(r_T=1/(2T)\), \(\delta_T=0\), and
\[
 e_T=T^{-1/2}+\frac1{2T}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{10}
\]
The radius restriction holds because
\[
 0<\rho=\frac\varepsilon8
 <\min\left\{1,\frac{\varepsilon h_-}{4D_2}\right\}
 =\min\left\{1,\frac\varepsilon4\right\}.
\tag{11}
\]

At \(\theta^*=0\), score outer products are diagonal, the third-arm term vanishes, and
\[
 E_{P^\dagger}[Y_t(1)^2]=\frac25,
 \qquad E_{P^\dagger}[Y_t(2)^2]=\frac12.
\tag{12}
\]
Using (1), (12), and the basin-covariance definition,
\[
 \Omega_1=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{2/5}{2/5},
 \frac{1/2}{1/4}\right)=\operatorname{diag}(1,2),
\tag{13}
\]
whereas
\[
 \Omega_2=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{2/5}{2/5},
 \frac{1/2}{1/6}\right)=\operatorname{diag}(1,3).
\tag{14}
\]
Both dominate \(I_2\), so basin nondegeneracy holds with \(\omega_-=1\).  Equations (1)--(14) verify every member condition in the finite-attractor class with constants common across horizons, hence \(P^\dagger\in\mathfrak P_T\) for every \(T\ge2\).

Since \(H=-I_2\),
\[
 V_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,2),
 \qquad V_2=\operatorname{diag}(1,3).
\tag{15}
\]
For \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\) and \(c=(1,0)^\top\),
\[
 c^\top V_1c=c^\top V_2c=c^\top\Sigma c=1,
 \qquad V_1\ne V_2.
\tag{16}
\]
Along every horizon sequence the covariance law is
\[
 \mu=\frac25\delta_{V_1}+\frac35\delta_{V_2}.
\tag{17}
\]
The contrastwise theorem and (16) give every-level validity for this contrast.  Equations (8), (15), and (17) make \(V_J\) nonconstant, so the matrixwise theorem rules out validity of one deterministic sandwich for all nonzero contrasts.  At the smallest allowed horizon \(T=2\), equation (7) holds for every assignment, including assignments omitting either active arm; this is the exact finite-instance stress test.  No finite-horizon coverage claim is made.

statements.statement:
Consider the bounded-noise Guo--Xu recursion with arbitrary fixed \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2>0\) and deterministic tie arm \(1\). Put \(p=99/100\), \(q=1/100\), and, for \((u,v)\in[q,p]^2\), define
\[
 h(u,v)=\left(\frac{u+16v}{2},\frac{17-u-16v}{2},
                 \frac{u-4v}{4},\frac{-3-u+4v}{24}\right).
\]
For \(t\ge1\), put \(D_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), \(N_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), and \(\Psi_t=(D_{t,1}/t,D_{t,2}/t,N_{t,1}/t,N_{t,2}/t)\). Then \(q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=O(t^{-1})\) almost surely, \(\Psi_t\) obeys an exact stochastic-approximation recursion with step \(1/(t+1)\), and its affine interpolation is a bounded perturbed solution, hence an asymptotic pseudotrajectory, of the closed convexified inclusion \(\dot\psi\in F(\psi)\) below. Writing \(\Delta(\psi)=n_1/d_1-n_2/d_2\), \(h_+=h(p,q)\), \(h_-=h(q,p)\), \(h_1=h(p,p)\), and \(h_2=h(q,q)\), its graph on \(d_1,d_2>0\) is
\[
 F(\psi)=
 \begin{cases}
  \{h_+-\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)>0,\\
  \{h_--\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)<0,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1<d_2,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1>d_2,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1=d_2.
 \end{cases}
\]
Every almost-sure normalized-state limit set is internally chain transitive for \(F\) and is contained in the computable parallelogram \(\mathcal C=\{h(u,v):(u,v)\in[q,p]^2\}\); the projected slope limit set is its continuous image under \((d_1,d_2,n_1,n_2)\mapsto(n_1/d_1,n_2/d_2)\).

The smaller inclusion having only \(h_+-\psi\), \(h_--\psi\), and \(\operatorname{co}\{h_+-\psi,h_--\psi\}\) on the switching surface is not a valid unconditional reduction of this recursion. If it were the limiting inclusion, its only internally chain-transitive sets would be the three singletons \(\{h_-\}\), \(\{h(u_0,1-u_0)\}\), and \(\{h_+\}\), where
\[
 u_0=\frac{47+\sqrt{4609}}{150},\qquad
 \frac{N_1}{D_1}=\frac{N_2}{D_2}
 =b_0:=\frac{\sqrt{4609}-91}{1224}
 \quad\text{at }h(u_0,1-u_0).
\]
The correct graph instead has an uncountable family of additional internally chain-transitive singleton equilibria. Explicitly, for
\[
 u\in[u_0,p],\qquad
 v(u)=\frac{3u+18-\sqrt{25u^2-228u+324}}{32},
\]
one has \(h(u,v(u))\in\mathcal C\), equal slope coordinates, first normalized Gram coordinate smaller than the second, and \(0\in F(h(u,v(u)))\). In particular,
\[
 v_*:=v(p)=\frac{2097}{3200}-\frac{3\sqrt{5457}}{640}
\]
gives an equilibrium \(h(p,v_*)\) distinct from \(h_-\), \(h(u_0,1-u_0)\), and \(h_+\). This continuum is an explicit internally-chain-transitive obstruction to a three-candidate conclusion from the standard differential-inclusion route.

For the actual recursion, on \(\mathcal L_+=\{\liminf_t(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}-\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})>0\}\) and \(\mathcal L_-=\{\limsup_t(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}-\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})<0\}\), respectively,
\[
 (\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top
 \longrightarrow
 \left(\frac{19}{46},-\frac{79}{3804}\right)^\top
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \left(-\frac{79}{634},\frac{19}{276}\right)^\top.
\]
Both events have probability bounded away from zero uniformly over \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), and the corresponding pathwise Cesaro errors converge to zero. If both slopes have a common-coordinate subsequential limit and \((u,v)\) is a simultaneous subsequential limit of the empirical conditional arm-\(1\) rates, then necessarily
\[
 u^2+12uv-21u-64v^2+72v=0.
\]
The relation \(v=1-u\), and hence the candidate \((u_0,b_0)\), is justified only if same-arm switching-layer occupation is separately excluded; the exact recursion does not provide that exclusion. Consequently, this argument proves neither finite almost-sure tail selection nor zero probability of switching-surface convergence. It also proves no compact-initial-set uniform attraction moduli \(r_T(K_0),\delta_T(K_0)\). These are dynamics-only conclusions: they assert neither membership in \(\mathfrak P_T\) nor applicability of any inference theorem.
statements.justification: The normalized sufficient-statistic recursion gives the strongest rigorous dynamics certificate currently available: it proves the two separated limits and exposes an uncountable switching-equilibrium obstruction in the correct limiting differential inclusion.
statements.gap: The differential-inclusion limit set need not be one of three candidates because the vanishing UCB bonus produces same-arm modes inside the shrinking switching layer. Actual selection within that layer, zero probability of switching convergence, and compact-initial-set uniform attraction still require quantitative escape and equicontinuity estimates not supplied here.
statements.consumer: The result prevents the bounded Guo--Xu analogue from being used as a certified two-basin inference witness while identifying the exact normalized-state graph and the additional dynamics that a future separatrix analysis must control.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(\mu _1=1/2\), \(\mu _2=1/12\), \(p=99/100\), \(q=1/100\), and \(C_{t,a}=\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}\).  The recursion in \(\textnormal{def:guoxu-recursion}\) gives, for every \(t\geq 1\),
\[
 D_{t,a}=1+\sum_{s=1}^t C_{s,a}X_s^2,\qquad
 N_{t,a}=\eta_{0,a}+\sum_{s=1}^t C_{s,a}X_s(\mu_a+\sigma_aR_{s,a}),\qquad
 \widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=\frac{N_{t,a}}{D_{t,a}}. \tag{1}
\]
The clipped randomization assigns either arm with conditional probability at least \(q\).  Because \(X_s\) is independent of \(\mathcal F_{s-1}\) and uniform on \(\{-4,1\}\),
\[
 E[C_{s,a}X_s^2\mid\mathcal F_{s-1}]
 \geq qE[X_s^2]=\frac{17}{200}. \tag{2}
\]
We first record the elementary bounded-martingale argument used repeatedly below.  Let \((U_s)\) be a scalar martingale-difference sequence with \(|U_s|\leq L\), and put \(S_n=\sum_{s=1}^nU_s\).  Expansion of the square and iterated conditional expectation make the cross terms zero, so \(E[S_n^2]\leq L^2n\).  For each integer \(m\geq1\), take \(\epsilon=1/m\) and define the event
\[
 A_m=\left\{\text{there exists }K<\infty\text{ such that }
 |S_{k^2}|\leq \frac{k^2}{m}\text{ for every }k\geq K\right\}. \tag{3}
\]
At \(n=k^2\), the pointwise inequality \(\mathbf 1\{|x|>a\}\leq x^2/a^2\) gives
\[
 P\left(|S_{k^2}|>\frac{k^2}{m}\right)
 \leq \frac{m^2E[S_{k^2}^2]}{k^4}
 \leq \frac{m^2L^2}{k^2}. \tag{4}
\]
Hence, for every \(K\),
\[
 P\left(\bigcup_{k\geq K}\left\{|S_{k^2}|>\frac{k^2}{m}\right\}\right)
 \leq m^2L^2\sum_{k\geq K}k^{-2}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Continuity from above of probability therefore yields \(P(A_m)=1\).  Now define the probability-one event
\[
 A_0=\bigcap_{m=1}^{\infty}A_m. \tag{5}
\]
On \(A_0\), for every \(m\geq1\),
\[
 \limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{|S_{k^2}|}{k^2}\leq\frac1m.
\]
Letting \(m\to\infty\) proves \(S_{k^2}/k^2\to0\) on \(A_0\).  Finally, if \(k^2\leq n<(k+1)^2\), boundedness of the increments gives
\[
 \frac{|S_n|}{n}
 \leq \frac{|S_{k^2}|}{k^2}+\frac{L(n-k^2)}{k^2}
 \leq \frac{|S_{k^2}|}{k^2}+\frac{L(2k+1)}{k^2}\longrightarrow0. \tag{6}
\]
Thus bounded-gap interpolation proves \(n^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^nU_s\to0\) almost surely.

Apply this result to \(C_{s,a}X_s^2-E[C_{s,a}X_s^2\mid\mathcal F_{s-1}]\).  Equations (1)--(2) yield
\[
 \liminf_{t\to\infty}\frac{D_{t,a}}t\geq\frac{17}{200},
 \qquad q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=D_{t,a}^{-1}=O(t^{-1})
 \quad\text{almost surely}. \tag{7}
\]
The same argument applies to \(C_{s,a}X_sR_{s,a}\): by the ordering in \(\textnormal{def:guoxu-recursion}\), the action is randomized before the reward innovation is observed, and that innovation is conditionally centered.  Hence
\[
 t^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^tC_{s,a}X_sR_{s,a}\longrightarrow0
 \quad\text{almost surely}. \tag{8}
\]
Moreover, (1) expresses each slope as a convex combination of its initial value \(\eta_{0,a}\) and the observed ratios \(Y_s(a)/X_s\), with weights \(1\) and \(C_{s,a}X_s^2\).  The envelope \(M_{\mathrm{GX}}\) therefore bounds both slopes.  Together with bounded \(X_s\) and bounded Rademacher rewards, this bounds every coordinate of \(\Psi_t\); by (7), both normalized Gram coordinates are eventually bounded away from zero.

Define
\[
 U_{t+1}=\bigl(C_{t+1,1}X_{t+1}^2,C_{t+1,2}X_{t+1}^2,
 C_{t+1,1}X_{t+1}Y_{t+1}(1),C_{t+1,2}X_{t+1}Y_{t+1}(2)\bigr).
\]
Dividing the four sufficient-statistic updates by \(t+1\) gives the exact stochastic-approximation recursion
\[
 \Psi_{t+1}-\Psi_t=\frac1{t+1}(U_{t+1}-\Psi_t). \tag{9}
\]
Conditional on \(\mathcal F_t\), let \(u_t\) and \(v_t\) be the arm-one assignment probabilities at contexts \(1\) and \(-4\), respectively.  Conditional centering of the rewards and direct averaging over the two equally likely contexts give
\[
 E[U_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t]=h(u_t,v_t), \tag{10}
\]
because the four coordinates on the right are
\[
 \frac{u_t+16v_t}{2},\qquad \frac{17-u_t-16v_t}{2},\qquad
 \mu_1\frac{u_t-4v_t}{2},\qquad
 \mu_2\frac{-3-u_t+4v_t}{2}.
\]
This is precisely the displayed formula for \(h\).

For \(\psi=(d_1,d_2,n_1,n_2)\), put \(\Delta(\psi)=n_1/d_1-n_2/d_2\).  At the current normalized state,
\[
 b_t:=\sqrt{q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}}-\sqrt{q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2}}
 =t^{-1/2}\bigl(d_{t,1}^{-1/2}-d_{t,2}^{-1/2}\bigr). \tag{11}
\]
The arm-one minus arm-two UCB index has the sign of \(\Delta(\Psi_t)+b_t\) at context \(1\), and the sign of \(b_t-\Delta(\Psi_t)\) at context \(-4\).  Equation (7) gives \(|b_t|=O(t^{-1/2})\).  Consequently, away from \(\Delta=0\), the two greedy choices are eventually opposite: \((u_t,v_t)=(p,q)\) for \(\Delta>0\), and \((u_t,v_t)=(q,p)\) for \(\Delta<0\).  On \(\Delta=0\), equation (11) has the sign of \(d_2-d_1\).  Thus both contexts make arm one greedy when \(d_1<d_2\), both make arm two greedy when \(d_1>d_2\), and the specified deterministic tie rule makes arm one greedy when \(d_1=d_2\).  The corresponding conditional means are \(h_1,h_2,h_1\), respectively.

This calculation gives the asserted closed convexified graph.  To verify the perturbation condition explicitly, observe that a same-arm mode can occur off the switching surface only if \(|\Delta(\Psi_t)|\leq |b_t|\).  On the eventual compact region already obtained, replace \(n_1\) by \(n_1-d_1\Delta(\Psi_t)\), leaving the other coordinates fixed.  The resulting point lies on \(\Delta=0\) and is within a fixed multiple of \(|\Delta(\Psi_t)|\) of \(\Psi_t\).  Therefore, for a deterministic \(c_0<\infty\) and all sufficiently large \(t\),
\[
 E[U_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t]-\Psi_t\in F^{\delta_t}(\Psi_t),
 \qquad \delta_t=c_0t^{-1/2}\longrightarrow0, \tag{12}
\]
where \(F^\delta\) denotes the graph enlargement.  The atoms \(h_+\) and \(h_-\) at every switching point make the graph closed under approach from the two open half-spaces; the atom \(h_1\), respectively \(h_2\), records approach within the switching layer when \(d_1<d_2\), respectively \(d_1>d_2\); and all four atoms at \(d_1=d_2\) close the remaining approaches.  Hence the displayed graph has nonempty compact convex values and is closed.  Its velocities have linear growth because its four atoms are fixed.  Outside a compact convex region containing the eventual trajectory, compose the atom correspondence with metric projection and retain the term \(-\psi\); this supplies a global extension with the same properties without changing the eventual dynamics.

Let \(M_{t+1}=U_{t+1}-E[U_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t]\) and \(\gamma_t=1/t\).  Each coordinate is a bounded martingale difference.  Stopping its weighted partial sum at the first crossing of \(\epsilon\) and using orthogonality of the stopped increments gives, for every coordinate and every \(j\),
\[
 P\left\{\sup_{k\geq2^j}\left|\sum_{s=2^j}^k\gamma_{s+1}M_{s+1}\right|>\epsilon\right\}
 \leq \frac{C}{\epsilon^2}\sum_{s=2^j}^{\infty}\gamma_{s+1}^2
 \leq\frac{C'}{\epsilon^22^j}. \tag{13}
\]
The probability that one of the events in (13) occurs for some \(j\geq J\) is at most \(C'\epsilon^{-2}\sum_{j\geq J}2^{-j}\), which tends to zero.  Thus the weighted martingale tails vanish almost surely, uniformly over every bounded interval of stochastic-approximation time.  Equations (9), (12), and (13), together with boundedness of \(\Psi_t\), verify the bounded-perturbed-solution hypotheses of \(\textnormal{lem:bhs-perturbed-limit-set}\).  That lemma makes the affine interpolation an asymptotic pseudotrajectory and makes its limit set internally chain transitive.

Let
\[
 \mathcal C=h([q,p]^2)=\operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1,h_2\}.
\]
Every velocity in \(F(\psi)\) is \(z-\psi\) for some \(z\in\mathcal C\).  If \(P_{\mathcal C}\psi\) is the Euclidean projection and \(V(\psi)=\operatorname{dist}(\psi,\mathcal C)^2\), the projection inequality gives, along every solution and for almost every time outside \(\mathcal C\),
\[
 \frac{d}{ds}V(\psi(s))
 =2(\psi-P_{\mathcal C}\psi)^\top(z-\psi)
 \leq-2\|\psi-P_{\mathcal C}\psi\|_2^2=-2V(\psi). \tag{14}
\]
If a solution starts in \(\mathcal C\), variation of constants writes it as a convex combination of its initial point and a weighted average of points \(z(s)\in\mathcal C\); hence \(\mathcal C\) is positively invariant.  Thus \(V\) is a continuous Lyapunov function for \(\mathcal C\), and \(V(\mathcal C)=\{0\}\) has empty interior.  By \(\textnormal{lem:bhs-lyapunov-ict}\), every internally chain-transitive normalized-state limit set lies in \(\mathcal C\).  Equation (7) keeps \(d_1,d_2\) positive on that limit set, so the slope projection \((d_1,d_2,n_1,n_2)\mapsto(n_1/d_1,n_2/d_2)\) is continuous there.  This proves the first paragraph of the claim.

We next identify exactly what the tempting two-mode inclusion would imply.  Let \(\mathcal C_0=\operatorname{co}\{h_-,h_+\}\) and write its points uniquely as \(h_-+\lambda(h_+-h_-)\), \(0\leq\lambda\leq1\).  Equivalently,
\[
 u=q+(p-q)\lambda,\qquad v=p-(p-q)\lambda=1-u. \tag{15}
\]
Cross-multiplication is legitimate because both Gram coordinates are positive, and direct expansion gives
\[
 \Delta(h(u,v))=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 f(u,v):=u^2+12uv-21u-64v^2+72v=0; \tag{16}
\]
indeed, after multiplication by the positive common denominator, the numerator of the slope difference is \(-5f(u,v)/48\).  Substitution of \(v=1-u\) yields \(f(u,1-u)=-75u^2+47u+8\).  Its unique root in \([q,p]\) is
\[
 u_0=\frac{47+\sqrt{4609}}{150},
\]
and substitution into either slope ratio gives \(b_0=(\sqrt{4609}-91)/1224\).

On \(\mathcal C_0\), the two-mode inclusion reduces to
\[
 \dot\lambda=-\lambda\quad(\lambda<\lambda_0),\qquad
 \dot\lambda=1-\lambda\quad(\lambda>\lambda_0),\qquad
 \dot\lambda\in[-\lambda_0,1-\lambda_0]\quad(\lambda=\lambda_0), \tag{17}
\]
where \(u_0=q+(p-q)\lambda_0\).  Distance squared to \(\mathcal C_0\) first confines every internally chain-transitive set to the segment by the argument of (14).  On the segment, the continuous function
\[
 W(\lambda)=
 \begin{cases}
 \lambda/\lambda_0,&0\leq\lambda\leq\lambda_0,\\
 (1-\lambda)/(1-\lambda_0),&\lambda_0\leq\lambda\leq1
 \end{cases}
\]
strictly decreases along every nonconstant solution outside \(\{0,\lambda_0,1\}\) and never increases from those three points.  Since \(W(\{0,\lambda_0,1\})=\{0,1\}\) has empty interior, \(\textnormal{lem:bhs-lyapunov-ict}\) puts every internally chain-transitive set inside \(\{0,\lambda_0,1\}\) with \(W\) constant.  The set \(\{0,1\}\) is not internally chain transitive: for \(\epsilon<1/3\), the solutions from its endpoints are constant, so no \((\epsilon,S)\)-chain contained in that two-point set can travel from one endpoint to the other.  Thus only the three asserted singletons are internally chain transitive for the smaller inclusion.

That smaller graph cannot approximate the recursion uniformly near the switching surface.  If \(\Delta=0\) and \(d_1<d_2\), equation (11) makes arm one greedy at both contexts and the conditional mean is \(h_1\).  But \(h_1\notin\mathcal C_0\): the affine map \((u,v)\mapsto h(u,v)\) is injective, every parameter pair on \(\mathcal C_0\) satisfies \(u+v=1\), and \(h_1\) corresponds to \((p,p)\), whose sum is \(2p\neq1\).  Compactness therefore gives \(\operatorname{dist}(h_1,\mathcal C_0)>0\).  The \(O(t^{-1/2})\) bonus cannot be discarded uniformly in the \(O(t^{-1/2})\) switching layer.

The extra internally chain-transitive sets of the correct graph are computable.  Solving (16) for its smaller \(v\)-root gives
\[
 v(u)=\frac{3u+18-\sqrt{25u^2-228u+324}}{32}. \tag{18}
\]
For \(u\in[u_0,p]\), substitution verifies \(f(u,v(u))=0\) and \(v(u_0)=1-u_0\).  Direct differentiation gives
\[
 v'(u)=\frac1{32}\left(3+\frac{228-50u}{2\sqrt{25u^2-228u+324}}\right)>0, \tag{19}
\]
because \(u\leq p<1\).  The elementary bounds \(67<\sqrt{4609}<68\) and \(73<\sqrt{5457}<74\) imply
\[
 0.23<v(u_0)<0.24,\qquad 0.308<v(p)<0.314.
\]
Consequently \(q<u,v(u)<p\), \(u+v(u)\geq1\), and
\[
 u+16v(u)\leq p+16v(p)<p+16(0.314)<6.014<\frac{17}{2}. \tag{20}
\]
The first two inequalities put \((u,v(u))\) in the triangle with vertices \((p,q),(q,p),(p,p)\), while (20) says that the first Gram coordinate of \(h(u,v(u))\) is smaller than the second.  Therefore
\[
 h(u,v(u))\in\operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1\},\qquad
 \Delta(h(u,v(u)))=0,\qquad 0\in F(h(u,v(u))). \tag{21}
\]
Each singleton in (21) is an equilibrium and hence internally chain transitive.  The map \(h\) is injective because the two linear forms \(u+16v\) and \(u-4v\) have nonzero determinant; the family is therefore uncountable.  At \(u=p\), equation (18) simplifies to
\[
 v(p)=\frac{2097}{3200}-\frac{3\sqrt{5457}}{640}=v_*,
\]
and the bounds above show that this equilibrium differs from the three two-mode candidates.  This proves the stated obstruction.

It remains to separate what the exact recursion itself establishes from what the enlarged inclusion merely permits.  Put \(\Delta_t=\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}-\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2}\).  On \(\mathcal L_+\), equation (7) makes the bonus vanish while \(\Delta_t\) is eventually bounded below by a positive constant.  Hence eventually arm one is greedy at context \(1\) and arm two at context \(-4\).  Applying the bounded martingale law proved above to the four context--action counts, and using (8) for the reward noise, gives
\[
 \frac1t(D_{t,1},D_{t,2},N_{t,1},N_{t,2})
 \longrightarrow h_+=\left(\frac{23}{40},\frac{317}{40},\frac{19}{80},-\frac{79}{480}\right). \tag{22}
\]
Equations (1) and (22) yield the first displayed slope limit.  The identical argument on \(\mathcal L_-\) gives
\[
 \frac1t(D_{t,1},D_{t,2},N_{t,1},N_{t,2})
 \longrightarrow h_-=\left(\frac{317}{40},\frac{23}{40},-\frac{79}{80},\frac{19}{480}\right), \tag{23}
\]
and hence the second displayed slope limit.  The limiting slope gaps are, respectively,
\[
 \frac{19}{46}+\frac{79}{3804}=
 \frac{37955}{87492}>0,
 \qquad
 -\frac{79}{634}-\frac{19}{276}=-\frac{16925}{87492}<0. \tag{24}
\]

We now prove the uniform positive-probability assertion rather than infer it from the differential inclusion.  Fix a sufficiently large even \(n\).  For the positive regime, prescribe a length-\(2n\) history consisting first of \(n\) observations with \(X=1,A=1\), then \(n\) observations with \(X=-4,A=2\), and prescribe equally many positive and negative Rademacher signs for each selected arm.  Each prescribed context has probability \(1/2\), each prescribed action has conditional probability at least \(q\), and each prescribed relevant sign has probability \(1/2\).  Thus this history has probability at least \((q/4)^{2n}\), uniformly over \(\eta_0\in[-1,1]^2\).  At its end the slopes are exactly
\[
 \frac{\eta_{0,1}+n/2}{1+n},\qquad
 \frac{\eta_{0,2}-n/3}{1+16n}, \tag{25}
\]
which converge uniformly in \(\eta_0\) to \(1/2\) and \(-1/48\), and both inverse Gram coordinates are \(O(n^{-1})\).

Consider after this prefix the reference policy that makes arm one greedy at context \(1\) and arm two greedy at context \(-4\).  After \(k\) further steps, its conditional-mean sufficient statistics are obtained by adding \(kh_+\) to the four terminal statistics in (25).  Each resulting armwise slope is a denominator-weighted average of its terminal slope and the corresponding ratio in \(h_+\).  By (24)--(25), there are constants \(\gamma_0>0\) and \(n_0<\infty\), independent of \(\eta_0\), such that for \(n\geq n_0\) these two reference slopes differ by at least \(3\gamma_0\) for every \(k\geq0\).  Their Gram coordinates are at least a fixed positive multiple of \(n+k\), so the absolute difference of their UCB bonuses is at most \(C(n+k)^{-1/2}\).  Increasing \(n_0\) makes this bound at most \(\gamma_0\).

Couple the actual rule and this reference rule with the same contexts, rewards, and randomization uniforms, and let \(\zeta\) be the first future occasion at which their greedy-arm maps differ.  If \(U^{\circ}_\ell\) is the sufficient-statistic increment at the \(\ell\)-th occasion after the prefix, define
\[
 M_k=\sum_{\ell=1}^k\mathbf 1\{\ell<\zeta\}\bigl(U^{\circ}_\ell-h_+\bigr).
\]
Because \(\{\ell<\zeta\}\) is known before the \(\ell\)-th post-prefix context and randomization, \((M_k)\) is a four-dimensional stopped martingale with a common bounded-increment constant depending only on the fixed \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2\).  The stopped-process maximal inequality and a union bound over the dyadic blocks \(2^jn\leq n+k<2^{j+1}n\) yield, for every fixed \(\gamma>0\),
\[
 P\left(\sup_{k\geq0}\frac{\|M_k\|_\infty}{n+k}>\gamma
 \mathrel{\Big|}\text{the prescribed prefix}\right)
 \leq \sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\frac{C}{\gamma^22^jn}
 =\frac{C_\gamma}{n}. \tag{26}
\]
Indeed, a crossing on the \(j\)-th block requires a stopped partial sum of size at least \(\gamma2^jn\), whereas orthogonality bounds its second moment by a constant times \(2^{j+1}n\), which gives the displayed summand.

Because all reference denominators are bounded below by a constant times \(n+k\), the ratio map is uniformly Lipschitz under the relative perturbation in (26).  Choose \(\gamma\) small enough both to preserve a positive constant lower bound for the perturbed denominators and to change the slope gap by at most \(\gamma_0\).  The same denominator bound makes the actual bonus difference \(O((n+k)^{-1/2})\); enlarge \(n_0\) once more so that it is at most \(\gamma_0\).  On the complementary event in (26), the actual slope gap is therefore at least \(2\gamma_0\), while its bonus difference is at most \(\gamma_0\).  At a putative first exit, the UCB index difference is consequently positive at context \(1\) and negative at context \(-4\), so the actual greedy arms still equal the reference greedy arms, a contradiction.  Thus \(\zeta=\infty\) on that event.  Equation (22), now applied under the reference policy, implies \(\mathcal L_+\).  Taking \(n\) still larger so that \(C_\gamma/n\leq1/2\) proves
\[
 \inf_{\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}}P_{\eta_0}(\mathcal L_+)
 \geq \frac12(q/4)^{2n}>0. \tag{27}
\]
For the negative regime, prescribe first \(n\) observations with \(X=-4,A=1\), then \(n\) with \(X=1,A=2\), again balancing the selected Rademacher signs.  The terminal slopes converge uniformly to \(-1/8\) and \(1/12\); the conditional-mean continuation adds \(kh_-\), and the second strict gap in (24) supplies the same stopped-martingale bootstrap.  Consequently
\[
 \inf_{\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}}P_{\eta_0}(\mathcal L_-)>0. \tag{28}
\]
On either event the corresponding slope sequence converges.  If \(\beta^+\) and \(\beta^-\) denote the two displayed deterministic limits, split each average at a fixed index after which every summand is at most an arbitrary \(\epsilon>0\); the fixed prefix divided by \(T\) vanishes.  Therefore, respectively,
\[
 \frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T\left\|\bigl(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2}\bigr)^\top-\beta^+\right\|_2\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T\left\|\bigl(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2}\bigr)^\top-\beta^-\right\|_2\longrightarrow0.
\]
This is the asserted pathwise Cesaro-error conclusion.

Finally, define the empirical context-specific arm-one rates
\[
 u_T=\frac{\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf1\{X_t=1,A_t=1\}}
 {\max\{1,\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf1\{X_t=1\}\}},\qquad
 v_T=\frac{\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf1\{X_t=-4,A_t=1\}}
 {\max\{1,\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf1\{X_t=-4\}\}}.
\]
The conditional arm-one probability at either context is always in \([q,p]\).  Applying the bounded martingale law to each context--action indicator after subtracting its predictable mean, and applying the same law to the centered context indicators, shows that each context count divided by \(T\) tends to \(1/2\) and that every subsequential limit of \((u_T,v_T)\) lies in \([q,p]^2\).  If along a common subsequence both slopes tend to a common coordinate and \((u_T,v_T)\to(u,v)\), then (1), (8), and the context-count law give
\[
 \frac1T(D_{T,1},D_{T,2},N_{T,1},N_{T,2})\longrightarrow h(u,v).
\]
The denominators in this limit are positive because \((u,v)\in[q,p]^2\).  Equality of the two limiting slope ratios is therefore equivalent, by (16), to
\[
 u^2+12uv-21u-64v^2+72v=0.
\]
